subject: Capacity expansion request — pool partitioning & sizing discussion
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta@clearwater.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference>
Cc: procurement@clearwater.ai
Date: 2026-07-28T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity expansion — Q3 rollout

Jordan —

Thanks for the quick demo last week. We have a product milestone in mid-September (multimodal launch) and our internal forecasts show token volume peaking and sustained increases during Q3. Procurement asked me to reach out formally: we need guidance on adding dedicated capacity to meet the new steady-load plus unpredictable spikes.

Key asks:
- Recommended GPU delta for +30% steady throughput with ability to absorb 2x traffic spikes for up to 2 hours/day.
- Options for staged commits vs. short-term burst pool.
- How Redwood would isolate our tenant (networking / KV cache warmers) while keeping latency SLOs.

I've attached our Q2 usage extract. Happy to jump on a call to walk through it.

Best,
Marta Lopez
Head of ML Ops, Clearwater AI

Attachments: Clearwater_ANR_usage_report_Q2.csv (CSV, 120KB)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference>
To: Marta Lopez <marta@clearwater.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-07-29T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity expansion — Q3 rollout

Marta —

Thanks for the data and context — congrats on the upcoming launch. Quick, pragmatic proposal below after a first pass through the CSV:

Summary recommendation
- Create a two-lane dedicated pool for Clearwater: a steady-state lane sized for +30% baseline (warm KV cache, pinned workers) and a burst lane that can auto-scale into reserved burst slots for 2-hour spikes.
- Start with a staged tranche: 40% of the total committed GPUs up-front, 30% in a 30-day canary tranche, and the remaining 30% after usage validation.
- Apply a small smoothing buffer (5–8% of provisioned GPUs) to absorb short tail spikes without routing to lower-tier models.

Operational/technical notes
- Isolation: we’ll pin network egress routes and dedicate the KV cache namespace to Clearwater so warmers maintain context across requests.
- Latency SLOs: keep <120ms p50 and <350ms p95 for your primary route; burst lane will accept slightly higher p95 but stay within 500ms during sustained spikes.
- Telemetry window: collect 14 days of per-client sequence-length histograms, tail-latency percentiles, and cache-hit rates before committing the final tranche.
- Fallback policy: if burst capacity saturates, traffic will gracefully overflow to a compatible quantized variant (same API surface) we pre-approve.

Pricing & commercial thoughts (high level)
- We’ll price the initial tranche at standard dedicated rates; can provide an interim month-to-month burst addendum for the canary period.
- If usage stabilizes above the committed baseline after 60 days, propose converting the burst addendum into the second tranche with a blended rate.

Next steps
1) Marissa / Karthik: can you validate feasibility for the two-lane pool and provide a draft tranche schedule? (cc'd)
2) Marta: if this sounds reasonable, we’ll follow with a technical runbook and a DocuSign for the initial tranche.

I attached a sketch of the partitioning layout and a draft tranche schedule for clarity. Happy to hop on a call this week to walk the plan.

—Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.inference | (415) 555-0182

Attachments: rdw-tranche-schedule-proposal.xlsx (Excel, 50KB); capacity-partitioning-diagram.png (PNG, 75KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-07-30T14:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity expansion — Q3 rollout

Jordan / team —

Reviewed Marta's usage and your notes. Quick ops feasibility and commercial tweak suggestions:

Ops/Provisioning items- We can carve a steady lane by reserving a contiguous subset of instances in the cluster (Nvidia H100/80 mix). Suggest starting with 12 H100-equivalent GPUs for the steady lane to hit +30% baseline based on the usage histogram.
- Burst lane: set an elastic reserve of 18 GPUs with soft preemption configured for low-priority batch jobs; this lets us honor the 2x spike headroom without impacting the rest of the fleet.
- Warmers: schedule KV cache priming during off-peak windows and run a small synthetic load to prefill frequently requested prefixes.

Commercial/Deal motion
- Tranche schedule OK but propose 35/25/40 split to reduce financial friction for procurement.
- Include an 8-week evaluation clause: if metrics (p50/p95, cache hit, throughput) meet thresholds we auto-apply tranche two at a 5% discount.

Questions for clarity
1) Marta — how important is strict network isolation vs. logical isolation? (we can do VPC peering + private endpoints or fully dedicated VPC for the committed pool).
2) Do you have an internal SLO for p95 latency we should aim for? You mentioned latency-sensitive workloads.

I can draft the initial SOW and the DocuSign wrapper once Jordan confirms the tranche split.

-Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference

Jordan / Marissa —

Thanks — that breakdown is helpful. A few quick answers:
- Network isolation: we need private endpoints and VPC-level isolation for the steady lane; burst lane can be logically isolated but must not cross our data egress boundary.
- Latency target: p95 < 400ms is our internal bar for the user-facing API.

We prefer the 35/25/40 tranche split Marissa proposed. Please send the draft SOW and the DocuSign link; procurement wants the canary/addendum language explicitly spelled out.

I'll schedule a 30-minute sync for Tuesday to finalize the runbook.

Best,
Marta
